stage04_google_sign_in_build.authority: Dor's choices in the stage04 Google sign-in session
stage04_google_sign_in_build.google_sign_in: Free original API of @react-native-google-signin/google-signin (16.1.5) with its Expo config plugin (iosUrlScheme). The ID token is exchanged with supabase.auth.signInWithIdToken({ provider: 'google' }).
stage04_google_sign_in_build.google_nonce: Supabase Google provider has Skip nonce check on. Reason: the free library cannot pass a nonce and the iOS Google SDK embeds its own hidden nonce. Supabase still verifies Google's signature, the audience (our Web and iOS client IDs) and expiry; lost is replay protection for a stolen token within its lifetime. Apple keeps its SHA-256 nonce. Rejected: paid Universal Sign-In; browser OAuth (shows the supabase.co address instead of the app name).
stage04_google_sign_in_build.google_client_ids: Google Cloud project with External consent screen in Testing (Dor as test user), an iOS client for com.doric2000.spanishforthebigtrip and a Web client whose secret lives only in the Supabase dashboard. Public client IDs in mobile/.env.local as EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID and EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID.
stage04_google_sign_in_build.layout_direction: Hebrew is the only declared iOS language (ios.infoPlist CFBundleLocalizations ['he'], CFBundleDevelopmentRegion 'he', which is what the expo-localization plugin writes), so React Native lays the app out right-to-left natively and the native Apple button reads Hebrew. Manual RTL emulation (row-reverse, flex-end, textAlign right) removed; rule in mobile/AGENTS.md, guarded by a test.
stage04_google_sign_in_build.native_packages_ahead_of_need: To avoid extra development builds Dor chose to install react-native-svg, expo-splash-screen, expo-haptics, expo-network and expo-image before the second build. Only expo-splash-screen is used now; the others stay unused until a screen needs them (setting aside the one-dependency-group-at-a-time rule for this build only).
stage04_google_sign_in_build.apple_button: Custom Hebrew Apple button instead of the native one (Dor, 2026-10-16): the native label follows the device language and read Spanish on Dor's Spanish-language iPhone. Follows Apple's custom-button rules: black, Apple logo, system font, 'Continue with Apple' in Hebrew. Sign-in still uses expo-apple-authentication signInAsync with the SHA-256 nonce.
stage04_google_sign_in_build.app_icon_and_splash: Logo D1 on the green background as the app icon (1024, no alpha) and the transparent D1 mark at width 320 on #21655B as the splash, approved in Figma section 68:320.

account_deletion.apple_token_revocation: Release gate before any public release: revoke the Sign in with Apple token on deletion through Apple's REST API with the .p8 key on a server (planned with the API in stage 05). Apple says apps 'should' do this.

dependency_audit.policy: Do not run npm audit fix --force: its fixes downgrade Expo (to 44) and React Native (to 0.72). Triage by where the vulnerable code runs and wait for Expo patch releases (Dependabot watches; SDK majors stay blocked).
dependency_audit.findings_2026_10_17: 30 warnings from 4 transitive advisories: braces (Metro, dev machine), node-forge (Expo CLI, dev machine), uuid (iOS build plugins, build time), decode-uri-component (expo-router query parsing, in the app; a malformed link can only hang the app it is opened in). Recheck after each Expo patch upgrade.

stage05_draft_units_in_development.authority: Dor chose option A in the stage05 chat ('נמשיך עם ההמלצה שלך, א')
stage05_draft_units_in_development.problem: GET /v1/units/:unitId returns only published revisions (content/api-contract.json), but unit 1A is a draft and C01 cannot be published until the whole chapter passes its checks.
stage05_draft_units_in_development.decision: A development-only setting ALLOW_DRAFT_UNITS=true in the local, Git-ignored api/.env lets the API return the latest draft revision. Without the setting the API returns only published revisions; a draft-only unit is 404.
stage05_draft_units_in_development.guardrails: The setting is never configured in a deployed environment (Vercel). A test proves that without it a draft-only unit returns 404. Drafts still go through projectUnit, so answers and review data never leave the server. This does not publish 1A or change the whole-chapter release rule.
